name: Tokelau

findings.builder: Bluearcus Technologies (4G mobile supplier/installer); Telecom Pasifika Samoa (tower foundations)
findings.financier: Government of Tokelau (General Fono capital injection)
findings.summary: Tokelau's first 4G mobile network launched on Fakaofo in May 2017, running a full LTE solution on Huawei radio equipment, installed by Bluearcus Technologies from November 2016 and funded by a General Fono capital injection.
findings.analyst_inference: Both sources carry near-identical wording and appear to reproduce the same Government of Tokelau release, so they are not treated as independent; corroborated set false, medium confidence rests on the opened S1 bulletin. The bulletin page's dateline reads 2012, apparently a typo for May 2017. Project value was a NZ$1.05m capital injection; not converted to USD because it is a funding allocation rather than a vendor contract value. Launch covered Fakaofo; extent on Atafu and Nukunonu and whether Huawei equipment is still in service were not confirmed, so still_current null.

findings.controller: Alcatel Submarine Networks (cable, repeater and branching-unit supplier and installer)
findings.local_actor: Teletok / Government of Tokelau (Nukunonu branch landing)
findings.financier: Governments of Tokelau and New Zealand (Nukunonu connection, jointly funded)
findings.summary: Tokelau's Nukunonu atoll was linked by branching unit to the Southern Cross NEXT trans-Pacific cable, landing celebrated in September 2021; ASN designed and installed the system, with commercial service expected July 2022. Tokelau and New Zealand jointly funded the connection.

sources.publisher: New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade

findings.analyst_inference: Under the equipment-vendor rule the controller is ASN (French, non-US/PRC), so pole third; the system owner Southern Cross Cable Network is also non-PRC. Coded tier 4 (cable landed, construction complete) because no opened source confirms the Tokelau branch entered commercial service; the July 2022 RFS date is for the overall system. MFAT and Samoa Observer likely relay the same official statement, but Lightwave is independent on the vendor and branching-unit facts.

findings.local_actor: Teletok (manages the cable for the Tokelau and New Zealand governments)
findings.financier: Governments of New Zealand and Tokelau (co-funded)
findings.summary: ASN was awarded a 250 km unrepeated domestic cable (OALC5, two fibre pairs) linking Atafu, Nukunonu and Fakaofo and interconnecting with Southern Cross NEXT; co-funded by New Zealand and Tokelau, managed by Teletok, RFS planned for 2021.

sources.publisher: Pacific Islands Research and Education Network (repost of ASN press release)

findings.analyst_inference: The PIREN page reposts ASN's own press release (corporate, S4), so only one opened S1-S3 source; not corroborated. Neither source names the contracting party or value. Completion of the domestic cable was not confirmed by any opened source (MFAT in 2021 still described it as coming in months), so tier held at 3 and still_current null.
